Apply T1 to its composition with the reduction, then directly specialize the query decider to `pairEncode x []`. This proves the statement after correcting findings 1–2. |
| T4 | `LogspaceReducible.polyTimeReducible` | Apply the received `ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.polyTimeComputable` to the same witness. `PolyTimeReducible` requires exactly that resulting computability property and the unchanged membership equivalence. |
| T5 | `NL_eq_LOGSPACE_of_nlComplete_mem_LOGSPACE` | Every member of `NL` reduces to the complete language, so T3 puts it in `LOGSPACE`. The converse inclusion is the supplied `LOGSPACE_subset_NL`. The reverse direction of the book's “iff” remark follows immediately from `NLComplete`'s membership conjunct and the equality. |
| T6 | `PATH_mem_NL` | Validate the complete encoding, check `s=t` immediately, then guess at most `n` edges with bounded vertex registers. A reachable target has a simple path of at most `n−1` edges, and all guessed walks stop at the cap. Space is logarithmic in the actual input length, including validation. |
| T7 | `PATH_NLComplete` | T6 proves membership. A bounded configuration graph retaining the output summary, with a single accepting target, gives a polynomial-size graph whose encoded bits and length are computable in logspace. Projection/lifting proves the membership equivalence; normalization and codec construction remain genuine named fill obligations. |
| T8 | `compl_PATH_mem_NL` | Accept malformed inputs. On valid instances, the induction in question 6 ensures that any surviving branch has the exact ball counts, while true certificates exist for every needed classification. The final exclusion test succeeds exactly when the target is unreachable, using bounded loops and logarithmic workspace. |
| T9 | `NL_eq_coNL` | For `B ∈ NL`, complement the membership equivalence of its reduction to `PATH` to get `Bᶜ ≤ₗ PATHᶜ`. T8 and nondeterministic downward closure give `Bᶜ ∈ NL`. Applying that implication to complements proves the reverse inclusion as well. |
| T10 | `NSPACE_compl_eq` | Compute the window from the constructibility witness and run the same counting algorithm on bounded configuration codes. Their lengths, all counters, and adjacency tests require `O(S n)` space by question 7. This constructs a decider for each complement; applying closure twice gives the displayed set equality. |
| T11 | `multLang_mem_LOGSPACE` | Validate all three canonical number fields and compute product columns with the bounded carry invariant in question 8. Compare every relevant output bit, reject excessive result length, and check that no carry remains. Zero operands and empty binary words need no extra space or hypothesis. |

**Answers to the eight numbered questions**

**1. Reducibility and the received divergences.** Both query languages and the polynomial output bound are present; none is inferred from the others. Reindexing `i` to `i+1` reconciles the zero-based and one-based conventions without changing the intended function class. The polynomial normalization does change a *literal*, all-input reading of the book's bound: the constant function with output `[false,false]` witnesses

\[
\operatorname{Set.univ}\le_l\{[\mathrm{false},\mathrm{false}]\}
\]

here, whereas `|f(x)| ≤ |x|^c` forces length at most one on every one-bit input and cannot witness this reduction. This is an already-declared, appropriate normalization of polynomial boundedness, not an undeclared discrepancy. Neither change damages composition or the intended complexity-theoretic results.

**2. Composition.** Suppose the bounds for `f,g` are `C(|x|+1)^c` and `D(|y|+1)^d`. Since `(|x|+1)^c ≥ 1`,

\[
\begin{aligned}
|g(f(x))|&\le D(|f(x)|+1)^d\\
&\le D\bigl((C+1)(|x|+1)^c\bigr)^d\\
&=D(C+1)^d(|x|+1)^{cd}.
\end{aligned}
\]

This includes zero constants/exponents and empty outputs. On a query word `w`, parse the aligned pair and validate the canonical index. Before storing its numerical value, compare its bit-length and, if necessary, its bits against the displayed polynomial bound: values at or beyond the bound make both queries false. Parsing an arbitrarily long index requires only counters of `O(log(|w|+2))` bits; an index small enough to retain has `O(log(|x|+2))` bits.

Compute `|f(x)|` by sequential length queries up to its polynomial bound. Simulate `g`'s appropriate query machine on `pairEncode (f x) (bits i)`: duplicated data positions use `f`'s bit query, the separator and index suffix use direct arithmetic, and endmarkers use the computed length. The virtual input length is polynomial in `|x|+1` after the index check. The suspended outer workspace, virtual head, inner query workspace, and counters occupy a constant number of logarithmic regions; calls reuse these regions rather than accumulating them. The two machines halt, and inner queries are deterministic. This supplies **both** `indexLang` memberships without storing `f(x)`.

**3. Transitivity, downward closure, polynomial refinement, collapse.** For the one-bit characteristic function `χ_C`, the exact query conditions on genuine pairs are

\[
\begin{aligned}
(\chi_C(x)).\operatorname{getD}(i,\mathrm{false})=\mathrm{true}
   &\iff i=0\ \land\ x\in C,\\
i<|\chi_C(x)|&\iff i=0.
\end{aligned}
\]

The first is decided by checking the paired shape/index and simulating the `C` decider on the decoded first component; the second is regular. For the last specialization step, directly simulate the resulting query decider on `dbl x ++ [false,true]`. A virtual head into this word needs `O(log(|x|+2))` bits and maps each doubled position back to one input bit. This elementary construction is independent of the general downward-closure theorem, avoiding circularity. T2, T4, and T5 then follow by the displayed membership equivalences and received inclusions.

**4. Encoding and `PATH`.** Applying `pairDecode` to equal encodings first gives equal unary words, hence equal vertex counts. Two further pair decodings give equal flattened matrices and endpoint bitstrings; `Nat.bits` injectivity gives equal endpoint values. For the now-common `n`, the matrix's entry at `u*n+v` recovers `A u v`, so function extensionality recovers the entire matrix.

Repeated use of `length_pairEncode` gives

\[
|\operatorname{encodePATH}(n,A,s,t)|
 =2n^2+2n+2|\operatorname{bits}(s)|+|\operatorname{bits}(t)|+6.
\]

Thus every instance is nonempty. `Fin 0` rules out a graph with designated vertices at `n=0`; it does not omit any legitimate empty-graph instance with two actual vertices. The zero-length path is legitimate: `GraphReach A s s` holds even without a loop. An empty endpoint word represents vertex zero unambiguously because the pair separator delimits it.

The validator must check three pair layers, an all-true nonempty unary field, exactly `n²` matrix bits, and canonical endpoint words denoting values below `n`. Canonical words are empty or end in `true`; merely interpreting padded binary numerals numerically is insufficient. Injectivity is useful for proving this validator exact and for lifting the decoded graph's result back to existential language membership. No total decoder fallback is needed.

**5. `PATH` membership and hardness.** Validation uses counters bounded polynomially in input length. After it succeeds, two vertex registers, a round counter, and matrix-address arithmetic remain logarithmic; when `n=1`, the counter still needs a constant number of cells. Test equality with the target before the first guessed edge, enforce guessed vertices `< n`, and halt every branch after at most `n` rounds.

For hardness, enumerate bounded configurations with blank tape outside the chosen window, including input-head position, state, tape contents/heads, and `OutSummary`. An adjacency test checks one possible transition and compares the resulting bounded code; it must not clamp an out-of-window successor into a valid vertex. From the real initial configuration, the space bound ensures every actual reachable configuration stays in the window. Conversely, step compatibility of the summary allows each coded path to be lifted to a real choice-word run. Halted state **and** `.accept` summary are required for acceptance.

An erase-and-park implementation is possible: record enough visited-boundary information during simulation, redirect halts into cleanup, erase the visited regions, return work heads to fixed origins, and return the input head to a fixed boundary. Preserve original output or track its summary without turning a dead output into acceptance. Boundary records and cleanup use `O(c₀ logSpace |x| + logSpace |x|)` space; count the **new** machine with a suitably enlarged constant. `cleanTM` is a model for part of this construction, not a supplied proof of it. Alternatively, a graph-level extra accepting sink would avoid machine cleanup, but would require revising the declared proof route, not the theorem.

The count is polynomial in `|x|+1` for a fixed machine and logarithmic window. Squaring it for an adjacency matrix remains polynomial. The paired encoding's length follows from question 4 and the endpoint-code lengths; its length query is arithmetic in the input length and index (the sketch's “in `i`” suppresses the input-length dependence). The default-false bit query must also handle every out-of-range index. None of this needs the P4.3 adjacency-CNF result.

**6. Counting and the single choice word.** For valid graphs, use the pack's balls `C_i` and counts `c_i`. Their defining recurrence is

\[
C_0=\{s\},\qquad
C_i=C_{i-1}\cup\{v:\exists u\in C_{i-1},\ A(u,v)=\mathrm{true}\}.
\]

Assume the preceding count is correct. A strictly increasing list of `c_{i-1}` vertices, each equipped with a verified path of length at most `i−1`, is a subset of `C_{i-1}` of the same size; hence it is exactly `C_{i-1}`. Therefore requiring, for every listed `u`, both `u ≠ v` and `A(u,v)=false` proves exactly `v ∉ C_i`. Notice the direction `u→v`.

At stage `i`, process **every** vertex `v=0,…,n−1`. Guess its membership flag and check either a length-at-most-`i` path or the preceding negative certificate; count the positive flags and compare that count with the proposed `c_i`. Starting from the verified `c_0=1`, induction forces every retained count to be correct. At the end, enumerate `c_n` distinct certified members of `C_n`, excluding `t`. This succeeds iff `t∉C_n`; finite-graph cycle removal gives `C_n` equal to the reachable set.

The stream order is: stage, next classified vertex, its flag, its positive path **or** its negative list of vertices and fresh positive paths, then the next classified vertex. Store the outer vertex and counter while consuming the inner path; discard each path after checking it. Later certificates may use different paths to the same vertex. No path or prior certificate bit is revisited, and the number of simultaneously stored registers is constant. Bound each list and path length, reject out-of-range values, and use fixed finite loop bounds even on dishonest choices. There are at most `O(n^4 log(n+2))` meaningful certificate bits; input rescans and deterministic microsteps still give a polynomial running bound in encoded input length.

A physical NDTM step consumes a choice bit even during deterministic work. Those bits can be ignored; successful certificate bits occupy the guessing steps, and the word is padded after halting to the common budget. Thus the direct construction needs no separate certificate-tape model. Finally, accept validator failure deterministically: `PATHᶜ` includes **all** malformed words, not just well-formed nonreachable instances.

**7. Complement equalities and the closure obligation.** The deterministic reduction remains unchanged under complementation:

\[
x\in B^c\iff f(x)\in C^c.
\]

For nondeterministic downward closure, retain the target machine's simulated configuration while running deterministic `f`-queries, then resume with the next actual nondeterministic choice. Each host branch projects to a target branch; every target branch can be realized by inserting ignored bits during the deterministic work. The target's all-branch halting budget on the fixed input `f(x)`, together with the finitely many halting query calls needed within that budget, gives a finite common host budget. Polynomial output length makes all workspace logarithmic. An appropriate standalone contract is

```lean
theorem mem_NL_of_logspaceReducible {B C : Language Bool}
    (h : B ≤ₗ C) (hC : C ∈ NL) : B ∈ NL
```

Its explicit promotion would improve the frozen audit surface; the present named-obligation policy does not require it as a condition of PASS.

For the general bound, write `n=|x|`, `s=c₀*S n`, `k=N.k`, and `q=Fintype.card N.State`. The supplied count obeys

\[
\begin{aligned}
N.\operatorname{configBound}(n,s)
 &=3(q+1)(n+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k\\
 &\le3(q+1)(n+2)2^{5ks+3k}\\
 &\le3(q+1)2^{(5kc_0+1)S(n)+3k+1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Here `3^r ≤ 2^(2r)`, `2s+1 ≤ 2^(s+1)`, and the bundled logarithmic floor supplies `n+2 ≤ 2^(S n+1)`. Thus vertex codes and counters have `O(S n)` bits, even though the number of vertices can be exponential. Compute and retain the binary window bound using the constructibility witness, then reuse the counting space. Constructibility supplies this effective bound; it is not additionally needed for the combinatorial induction. The separately bundled logarithmic floor pays for input addressing and constant overhead. No monotonicity of `S` is required.

For the exact set equality, closure sends a member of the right-hand side to a member of the left-hand side. If `L` belongs to the left, apply closure to `Lᶜ` and use `(Lᶜ)ᶜ=L` to obtain membership on the right. Empty inputs are harmless because `S 0 ≥ logSpace 0 = 1`.

**8. Multiplication.** Pair injectivity and binary injectivity make the existential language exactly the canonical triples satisfying the product equation. In particular,

\[
\operatorname{pairEncode}([],\operatorname{pairEncode}([],[]))=0101\in\mathrm{multLang};
\]

the whole empty word is not a member. Both `a=0` and `b=0` require the product field to be empty.

For input bits `a_p,b_q`, maintain the carry and column sum via

\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{carry}_0&=0,\\
\operatorname{column}_j&=\sum_{p+q=j}a_p b_q,\\
\operatorname{productbit}_j&=(\operatorname{carry}_j+\operatorname{column}_j)\bmod2,\\
\operatorname{carry}_{j+1}&=\left\lfloor
 (\operatorname{carry}_j+\operatorname{column}_j)/2\right\rfloor.
\end{aligned}
\]

The correctness invariant is

\[
\sum_{r<j}2^r\operatorname{column}_r
 =\sum_{r<j}2^r\operatorname{productbit}_r+2^j\operatorname{carry}_j.
\]

If `m` is the total encoded input length, then `column_j ≤ m`; induction gives `carry_j ≤ m`, and the temporary sum is at most `2m`. All counters and arithmetic therefore use `O(log(m+2))` bits. Validate canonical words, reject a result field longer than the sum of the two operand bit-lengths, and compare through that many columns using zero for missing result bits. This handles products whose bit-length is smaller than the maximum column count, including zero; “simultaneous end” must not mean that these lengths are always equal.

**Adversarial instantiations**

Bitstrings in this table spell Boolean lists with `0=false`, `1=true`.

| Test | Instantiation and calculation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Empty word `[]`. Every graph encoding has length at least 10; every multiplication encoding at least 4. | Outside `PATH` and `multLang`; inside `PATHᶜ`. |
| A2 | `n=1`, no edges, `s=t=0`; encoding `1101000101`. | In `PATH` by the zero-edge path. A walk requiring a first edge would be wrong. |
| A3 | Same graph with its self-loop; encoding `1101110101`. | Still in `PATH`, with no encoding collision with A2. |
| A4 | Attempted zero-vertex shape `010101` (three nested empty pairs). | No `Fin 0` endpoint exists; reject as an instance and accept in the complement. |
| A5 | A2 with endpoint zero encoded as `[false]` instead of `[]`. | Numerically suggestive but noncanonical: outside `PATH`, inside its complement. |
| A6 | Two vertices, only edge `0→1`. | `(s,t)=(0,1)` is reachable; `(1,0)` is not. Reversing adjacency in the negative certificate fails this test. |
| A7 | `(a,b)=(0,0)` gives `0101`; `(0,1)` gives `011101`. | Both in `multLang`. Empty fields are genuine zero representations. |
| A8 | Triple `⟨0,b,1⟩`, or any correct product field with an extra terminal `false` bit. | Both rejected: the first arithmetically, the second by canonical validation. |
| A9 | `NLComplete ∅` would require the universal language to reduce to the empty language; `NLComplete Set.univ` would require the empty language to reduce to the universal language. | Both impossible. Both source languages have constant-output deciders in `NL`, so the hardness quantifier is not vacuous. |
| A10 | `f x=[]` for every `x`. Its two query languages are empty, and its length bound has `C=0`. | A valid implicit function. It reduces exactly `B=Set.univ` when `[]∈C`, and exactly `B=∅` otherwise. |
| A11 | One-bit characteristic output queried at index 1. | Length query is false for every input, witnessing finding 1. |
| A12 | A bounded function outputs `[false]` on an undecidable language and `[]` otherwise. | Its bit language is empty, but its length query at index 0 is undecidable. The received third conjunct correctly excludes it. |
| A13 | A machine emits `true`, then `false`, then halts. | Its live `.accept` summary is not acceptance; the terminal summary is `.dead`. Hardness must require halting and preserve the summary. |
| A14 | Constant two-bit reduction from `Set.univ` to the singleton containing `00`. | Allowed here, excluded by the literal `length(x)^c` bound on one-bit inputs; confirms the declared normalization's exact effect. |
| A15 | `S=logSpace`, including input length zero; also a zero-work-tape source machine. | The complement construction has positive administrative space available. A zero-tape source does not force its simulator to use zero tapes. |

As independent finite checks, a direct Python translation verified 961 pair round-trips with no collisions; all 4,674 graph encodings for `1≤n≤3`, their lengths, decoding, and injectivity; 13,954 local inductive-counting cases; and 12,288 multiplication checks with `0≤a,b<64` (correct product, padded representation, and incorrect product). All passed. These checks are diagnostic evidence, not Lean tests or substitutes for the general arguments above.

**Suggested additive sanity contracts**

No existing frozen statement needs alteration. Useful permanent checks are: the exact `encodePATH` length; recovery/injectivity of its components; `encodePATH n A s t ∈ PATH ↔ GraphReach A s t`; reflexive membership; exclusion of the empty word; acceptance of every malformed word by `PATHᶜ`; membership of the zero-product encodings; the fixed-index `indexLang` specialization; and the proposed nondeterministic downward-closure contract. The codec, normalization, and compiler proofs remain fill obligations, not new conclusions certified by this report.

**Notation glossary.** `|x|` is word length; `[]` is the empty word; `bits` is `Nat.bits`; `dbl` repeats each bit; `≤ₗ` is the supplied logspace reducibility; `Lᶜ`/`L^c` is language complement; `Set.univ` is all Boolean words. `χ_C` is the one-bit characteristic function of `C`. `C,c,D,d` are the respective output-bound constants/exponents for `f,g`. `C_i,c_i` are the reachable ball and its size. In the configuration calculation, `n=|x|`, `s=c₀S(n)`, `k` is the tape count, and `q` the live-state count. In the multiplication calculation, `m` is encoded input length, `a_p,b_q` are operand bits, and `column_j`, `carry_j`, `productbit_j` are the displayed grade-school quantities. All other identifiers are those of the supplied pack.

**Environment disclosure.** This executor's PID namespace makes Lean's
`/proc/<own-pid>/exe` lookup fail even though `/proc/self/exe` works. A local
`readlink` compatibility shim redirects only the exact lookup for the calling
process to `/proc/self/exe`; all other calls and permissions are unchanged.
It does not alter Lean, the kernel, sources, the checker, proof terms, diagnostics,
or exit statuses. The source is included as
`evidence/proc-self.c.txt`; no binary or executable wrapper is delivered, and
the patch/bundle has no shim dependency. In a normal Lean installation, run the
repository checker directly. The axiom probe is retained as
`evidence/C1aAxioms.lean.txt`; its temporary checkout copy was removed.

`sorry` terms in the three owned modules, and none of the 15 axiom prints
uses `sorryAx`.

## Filled targets and binding proof routes

| ID | Declaration | Proof route |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | `Complexity.evenLang_mem_LOGSPACE` | Exported zero-tape scanner, shared bridge, then space monotonicity to `0 * logSpace n`. |
| Z1 | `Turing.FinTM.k_le_spaceUsed` | Time zero makes every visited image nonempty; sum the lower bound one. |
| Z2 | `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.k_eq_zero_of_exists_zero` | Instantiate at `List.replicate n false`, use Z1 and `omega`. |
| Z3 | `Complexity.SPACE_eq_zero_of_exists_zero` | Z2 at the scaled bound, the shared bridge, and `SPACE.mono` for the reverse inclusion. |
| Z4 | `Complexity.SPACE_id_eq_SPACE_zero` | Z3 at the zero length. |
| Z5 | `Complexity.SPACE_succ_of_pos` | `SPACE.mono` and `SPACE.mono_const (a := 2)`, using positivity at every length. |
| Z6 | `Complexity.SPACE_succ_eq_max_one` | The same two shared monotonicity results and the `max 1` inequalities. |
| Z7 | `Turing.pairEncode_bits_inj` | Cite `pairEncode_injective` and `Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective`. |
| Z8 | `Complexity.trueLang_mem_SPACE_zero` | Private one-step constant machine and the shared zero-tape bridge. |
| Z9 | `Complexity.evenLang_mem_SPACE_zero` | The Examples exports and shared bridge directly. |
| Z10 | `Complexity.exists_zeroTape_const_oneStep` | Reuse the same private constant machine and contract. |
| Z11 | `Complexity.exists_zeroTape_parity_decider` | Reuse the two Examples exports. |
| C1 | `Complexity.CounterProg.sim_run_of_regs_le` | Induction, one-step `sim_run` at headroom one, and composition of runs. |

The parity state starts at `true` (even), stays unchanged on `false`, and toggles
on `true`. Its single private invariant records the parity of
`(x.take j).count true`, head position `j + 1`, and empty output. At the right
blank it emits that state and halts, proving the `n + 1` contract, including the
empty input. This is bit parity. E1 uses the bridge directly and imports no
ZeroSpace module. The constant machine emits and halts in one transition.

**C1 step discharge.** In the successor case, call
`sim_run P x l₀ (B + 1) 1 s hp ...`. The hypothesis `hB 0` and `run_zero`
supply the required headroom, giving a cost at most
`1 * (2 * (B + 1) + 3) = 2 * B + 5`; the received `sim_run` handles halted
states. The suffix starts at `run P x s 1`; `step_pos_le` supplies its position
bound, and `hB (1 + j)` with `run_add` supplies its reachable-register bounds.
`runFrom_add`/`run_add` compose the witnesses and `nlinarith` closes the total
bound. The frozen statement remains `t * (2 * B + 5)`. There is no additional
register hypothesis on the final state and no new corollary.

| Public, required export | `Complexity.evenScanTM` | The one zero-work-tape, two-state parity scanner. |

| Private | `Complexity.evenScanTM_prefix` | The single prefix invariant for that scanner. |
| Private | `Complexity.constTrueTM` | The one zero-work-tape, one-state constant-true machine. |
| Private | `Complexity.constTrueTM_computesInTime` | Its one-step contract on every input. |

### Environment recovery

The initial run was interrupted by the network/session hiccup, so the baseline
resumed at its first unfinished module. The raw baseline log preserves that
resume and the subsequent failed import attempts. Unchanged CodeParser and
SAT compiled artifacts required regeneration before MathlibBridge and
Cook–Levin Hardness respectively could import them; the same check script
then passed. No repository source was edited to resolve either issue.

The first final axiom pass exposed an old admitted CounterProgRun artifact.
Regenerating it produced the proved target without `sorryAx`. To prevent stale
artifact interference, the definitive owned/replay sweep and axiom audit used
an isolated output tree seeded from this task's checked dependencies, with
`TCSLIB_OLEANS` set for the unchanged check script. The superseded first sweep
and axiom logs are retained under `evidence/`; the root logs are the final
passing runs.

This sandbox's process and procfs namespaces differ. A small runtime
compatibility shim redirects only Lean's own `/proc/<getpid()>/exe` readlink
to `/proc/self/exe`, allowing the pinned binary to locate its installation.
It changes no Lean implementation, kernel check, or proof. Its C source and
the environment/version evidence are included for transparency. All checks
ran inside the existing sandbox. The final sweep has no crashes or failures.

`SHA256SUMS` covering every other packaged file.

`refs/heads/fill/ch34-c1b`. With that base available, `git bundle verify`

commit. No checkout or integration into a remote branch was performed.

**Every new private declaration** is listed here; all are proved and have Proof sketches.

| File | Private declaration | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `OracleNondeterministic.lean` | `Turing.toOracleNDTM_stepWith` | The batch's only unfolding comparison of `stepWith` against `step`; halted/query/ordinary cases |
| `OracleNondeterministic.lean` | `Turing.runWith_headBlank` | Induction on the choice word from an arbitrary configuration and radius; cites the deterministic movement and write-locality lemmas through E2 |
| `OracleNondeterministic.lean` | `Turing.queryString_length_le_of_blank` | A blank query cell bounds extraction using `Nat.find_le` |
| `OracleAgreement.lean` | `Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_query_agree` | Core (i): query-answer agreement, with the public off-query lemma |
| `OracleAgreement.lean` | `Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree` | Core K: the single branch-prefix locality induction |
| `OracleAgreement.lean` | `Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_replicate` | Core (iii): deterministic runs as prefixes of constant choice words, citing target 1 |
| `OracleAgreement.lean` | `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_query_agree` | Factors the constant-word specialization shared by targets 8 and 9; no second induction |
| `OracleAgreement.lean` | `Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_filtered_queries` | One filter-map membership argument for targets 5 and 10 |

Target 1 inducts on the choice word after the private step identity. E2 reuses that identity at `fixChoice`; no other per-step nondeterministic fact is re-proved by unfolding `stepWith`. E4's generalization advances the radius once and calls the induction hypothesis on the suffix. E5 uses the cell at the branch length as the blank witness.

The inclusions retain the exact multiplicative constant and exponent. Target 3 establishes one local equality for every branch of the input's budget, uses the replicated-false word for member acceptance, and excludes acceptance of a nonmember by its `[false]` output. There is no new declaration in `Classes.lean`.

K splits `take (s+1)` into `take s` and the next bit, uses `runWith_append`, identifies the prefix configurations, and transports core (i)'s conclusion by E2. The four locality targets all reuse K. The two deterministic targets share its constant-word specialization. The two membership bounds share a single index-extraction lemma. The query-count bound cites `List.length_filterMap_le` and `List.length_range`.

 theorem DTIME_subset_SPACE (T : ℕ → ℕ) : DTIME T ⊆ SPACE T := by
-  sorry
+  classical
+  by_cases hzero : ∃ n, T n = 0
+  · rw [DTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero hzero]
+    exact Set.empty_subset _
+  have hpos (n : ℕ) : 1 ≤ T n := by
+    by_contra hn
+    exact hzero ⟨n, by omega⟩
+  rintro L ⟨c, M, hM⟩
+  refine ⟨M.k * c + M.k, M, fun x => ?_⟩

+  calc
+    M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) (c * T x.length)
+        ≤ M.k * (c * T x.length + 1) := M.tm.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ _ _
+    _ = M.k * c * T x.length + M.k := by
+      rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one, Nat.mul_assoc]
+    _ ≤ M.k * c * T x.length + M.k * T x.length :=
+      Nat.add_le_add_left
+        (by simpa only [Nat.mul_one] using Nat.mul_le_mul_left M.k (hpos x.length)) _
+    _ = (M.k * c + M.k) * T x.length := (Nat.add_mul _ _ _).symm

 `Complexity.DTIME_subset_SPACE`, then `Set.iUnion_mono` across the unions

 larger bound: `c · s₁ n ≤ c · s₂ n` pointwise (`Nat.mul_le_mul_left`), and only

 theorem NSPACE.mono {s₁ s₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, s₁ n ≤ s₂ n) : NSPACE s₁ ⊆ NSPACE s₂ := by
-  sorry
+  intro L hL

+  refine ⟨T, hhalt, ?_, hacc⟩
+  intro w hw
+  exact (hsp w hw).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h x.length))

 [AB09, Theorem 4.2, second inclusion]

@@ -44,6 +47,81 @@ open Turing
 def evenLang : Language Bool :=
   {x | x.count true % 2 = 0}
 
+/-- The parity scanner uses no work tapes and two live states: `true` means
+that the consumed prefix has even parity. It toggles on `true`, keeps its
+state on `false`, and emits its state and halts at the right blank.
+[AB09, Example 4.7]
+
+The missing catalog row is a finite-state scanner with a final verdict:
+`transducer_run` halts silently, so its contract cannot emit this bit. -/
+def evenScanTM : FinTM Bool where
+  k := 0
+  State := Bool
+  tm :=
+    { q₀ := true
+      tr := fun q inp _ => match inp with
+        | some b => FinTM.controlAction .pos (some (if b then !q else q))
+        | none => ⟨0, fun i => i.elim0, some q, none⟩ }
+
+/-- After consuming a prefix, the scanner stores its even-parity bit, points
+to the next input position, and has emitted nothing.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the prefix length. The initial state records
+zero true bits. Reading the next bit preserves or toggles parity, advances
+the head once, and emits nothing. The prefix-count update is the count of
+an appended singleton; residues modulo two justify the toggle. -/
+private theorem evenScanTM_prefix (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ x.length) :
+    (evenScanTM.tm.runFrom (evenScanTM.tm.initCfg x) j).state =
+        some (decide ((x.take j).count true % 2 = 0)) ∧
+      (evenScanTM.tm.runFrom (evenScanTM.tm.initCfg x) j).inputPos.val = j + 1 ∧
+      (evenScanTM.tm.runFrom (evenScanTM.tm.initCfg x) j).output = [] := by
+  induction j with
+  | zero => simp [evenScanTM]
+  | succ j ih =>
+    obtain ⟨hq, hp, ho⟩ := ih (by omega)
+    have hlt : j < x.length := by omega
+    have hs := FinTM.inputSymbol_at
+      (evenScanTM.tm.runFrom (evenScanTM.tm.initCfg x) j) j (by omega) hp
+    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hlt] at hs
+    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
+    unfold MultiTapeTM.step
+    rw [hq]
+    simp only [evenScanTM, hs, FinTM.controlAction, Action.apply]
+    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · rw [List.take_succ_eq_append_getElem hlt, List.count_append]
+      cases x[j] with
+      | false => simp
+      | true =>
+        have hm := Nat.mod_lt ((x.take j).count true) (by decide : 0 < 2)
+        by_cases he : (x.take j).count true % 2 = 0
+        · simp [Nat.add_mod, he]
+        · have he' : (x.take j).count true % 2 = 1 := by omega
+          simp [Nat.add_mod, he']
+    · rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by omega)]
+      simpa using hp
+    · simpa using ho
+
+/-- The zero-work-tape scanner decides the even-parity language within
+`n + 1` steps on every input of length `n`. [AB09, Example 4.7]
+
+**Proof sketch.** Apply the prefix invariant to the whole input. The next
+symbol is the right blank, so one more transition emits the even-parity
+indicator and halts. This includes the empty input. -/
+theorem evenScanTM_decidesInTime :
+    evenScanTM.DecidesInTime evenLang fun n => n + 1 := by
+  intro x
+  obtain ⟨hq, hp, ho⟩ := evenScanTM_prefix x x.length le_rfl
+  have hs := FinTM.inputSymbol_at
+    (evenScanTM.tm.runFrom (evenScanTM.tm.initCfg x) x.length) x.length le_rfl hp
+  simp only [List.getElem?_length] at hs
+  apply (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr
+  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
+  unfold MultiTapeTM.step
+  rw [hq, hs]
+  simp only [evenScanTM, Action.apply]
+  rw [ho]
+  simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, evenLang]
+
 /-- **Parity is decidable in logarithmic space** — in fact in constant space,
 which the `c · logSpace n` budget absorbs since `logSpace n ≥ 1`.
 [AB09, Example 4.7]
@@ -60,6 +138,10 @@ parity of the consumed prefix — with the final emission
 `[Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator evenLang x]` at the input boundary, halting at
 time `n + O(1)`. -/
 theorem evenLang_mem_LOGSPACE : evenLang ∈ LOGSPACE := by
-  sorry
+  refine ⟨0, evenScanTM, ?_⟩
+  refine (FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero (M := evenScanTM) rfl ?_).mono
+    (fun _ => Nat.zero_le _)
+  intro x
+  exact ⟨x.length + 1, evenScanTM_decidesInTime x⟩

+/-- Two oracle steps agree if the oracles agree on the current query whenever
+the current state is the query state.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Away from the query state cite oracle independence. At the
+query state, equal membership answers select the same successor state. -/
+private theorem step_eq_of_query_agree (M : OracleTM k Symbol State)
+    (O O' : Language Symbol) {input : List Symbol}
+    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input)
+    (h : cfg.state = some M.qQuery → (queryString cfg ∈ O ↔ queryString cfg ∈ O')) :
+    M.step O cfg = M.step O' cfg := by
+  classical
+  by_cases hq : cfg.state = some M.qQuery
+  · have answer := propext (h hq)
+    simp only [step, hq, answer]
+  · exact step_eq_of_ne_qQuery O O' hq
+
+/-- Agreement on the queries actually submitted along a choice word under the
+first oracle makes every prefix configuration coincide under the two oracles.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the prefix length. Split the next prefix into the
+old prefix and its next bit. The induction hypothesis identifies the starting
+configurations; the fixed-choice bridge and step agreement identify their next
+steps, using the query hypothesis along the first run. This single induction
+also serves deterministic runs through their constant-choice embedding. -/
+private theorem runWith_take_eq_of_agree (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State)
+    (O O' : Language Symbol) (x : List Symbol) (w : List Bool)
+    (h : ∀ s < w.length,
+      (N.runWith O (w.take s) (N.initCfg x)).state = some N.qQuery →
+        (queryString (N.runWith O (w.take s) (N.initCfg x)) ∈ O ↔
+          queryString (N.runWith O (w.take s) (N.initCfg x)) ∈ O')) :
+    ∀ s ≤ w.length,
+      N.runWith O (w.take s) (N.initCfg x) = N.runWith O' (w.take s) (N.initCfg x) := by
+  intro s
+  induction s with
+  | zero => intro _; rfl
+  | succ s ih =>
+    intro hs
+    have before : s < w.length := Nat.lt_of_succ_le hs
+    rw [List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem before, Option.toList_some,
+      OracleNDTM.runWith_append, OracleNDTM.runWith_append]
+    change N.stepWith O w[s] (N.runWith O (w.take s) (N.initCfg x)) =
+      N.stepWith O' w[s] (N.runWith O' (w.take s) (N.initCfg x))
+    rw [← ih (Nat.le_of_lt before)]
+    have next := step_eq_of_query_agree (N.fixChoice w[s]) O O' _ (h s before)
+    simpa only [← OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step] using next
+

+    (p : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (t : ℕ)

+  have before := List.mem_range.mp hs

+/-- Fixing the choice bit of a nondeterministic oracle machine gives a

+def OracleNDTM.fixChoice (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State) (b : Bool) :
+    OracleTM k Symbol State := ⟨N.q₀, N.qQuery, N.qYes, N.qNo, N.tr b⟩
+
+/-- A nondeterministic oracle step under bit `b` is the deterministic step of

+fixed-choice machine; the nondeterministic steps are definitionally equal. -/
+theorem OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State)
+    (O : Language Symbol) (b : Bool) (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) :
+    N.stepWith O b cfg = (N.fixChoice b).step O cfg :=

+and blank beyond the enlarged radius `n + w.length` after a branch run.

+private theorem runWith_headBlank (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State)
+    (O : Language Symbol) (w : List Bool) (n : ℕ)
+    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input)
+    (hpos : ∀ i, |cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ (n : ℤ))
+    (hblank : ∀ i (z : ℤ), (n : ℤ) ≤ |z| → cfg.workTapes i z = none) :
+    (∀ i, |(N.runWith O w cfg).workTapePos i| ≤ ((n + w.length : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
+      ∀ i (z : ℤ), ((n + w.length : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ |z| →
+        (N.runWith O w cfg).workTapes i z = none := by
+  induction w generalizing n cfg with
+  | nil => simpa only [OracleNDTM.runWith_nil, List.length_nil, Nat.add_zero] using
+      And.intro hpos hblank
+  | cons b w ih =>
+    have nextPos : ∀ i, |(N.stepWith O b cfg).workTapePos i| ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
+      intro i
+      rw [OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step]
+      have move := (N.fixChoice b).workTapePos_step_le O cfg i
+      have old := hpos i
+      rw [abs_le] at move old ⊢
+      omega
+    have nextBlank : ∀ i (z : ℤ), ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ |z| →

+        rw [← heq] at old

+      exact hblank i z (by omega)
+    have suffix := ih (n + 1) (N.stepWith O b cfg) nextPos nextBlank
+    simpa only [OracleNDTM.runWith_cons, List.length_cons,
+      Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm 1 w.length] using suffix

+/-- After an initialized branch run, every work head is within the number of

+theorem OracleNDTM.runWith_workTapes_invariant (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State)
+    (O : Language Symbol) (x : List Symbol) (w : List Bool) :
+    (∀ i, |(N.runWith O w (N.initCfg x)).workTapePos i| ≤ (w.length : ℤ)) ∧
+      ∀ i (z : ℤ), (w.length : ℤ) ≤ |z| → (N.runWith O w (N.initCfg x)).workTapes i z = none := by
+  simpa only [Nat.zero_add] using
+    runWith_headBlank N O w 0 (N.initCfg x) (by intro i; simp)
+      (by intro i z _; rfl)
+
+/-- A blank at the nonnegative query-tape cell `n` bounds the extracted query
+length by `n`, from any configuration.
+
+**Proof sketch.** The least blank exists with witness `n` and is at most `n`.
+Filtering the preceding range cannot increase its length. This is requested
+for the shared home `Oracle.lean`. -/
+private theorem queryString_length_le_of_blank (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input)
+    (n : ℕ) (h : cfg.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ) = none) :
+    (OracleTM.queryString cfg).length ≤ n := by
+  classical
+  rw [OracleTM.queryString, dif_pos ⟨n, h⟩]
+  refine (List.length_filterMap_le _ _).trans ?_
+  simpa using (Nat.find_le (h := ⟨n, h⟩) h)
+
+/-- The query string after an initialized nondeterministic branch run has length
+at most the length of the choice word. [AB09, proof of Theorem 3.7, branchwise]
+
+**Proof sketch.** The initialized invariant keeps the query cell at the branch
+length blank. The blank-cell bound then bounds the extracted query. -/
+theorem OracleNDTM.queryString_runWith_length_le (N : OracleNDTM k Symbol State)
+    (O : Language Symbol) (x : List Symbol) (w : List Bool) :
+    (OracleTM.queryString (N.runWith O w (N.initCfg x))).length ≤ w.length := by
+  exact queryString_length_le_of_blank _ w.length
+    ((N.runWith_workTapes_invariant O x w).2 _ _ (le_abs_self _))
 
 /-- A bundled deterministic oracle machine as a bundled nondeterministic one, with
 the same tapes, state type, and special states. -/
--

-/-- **Zermelo determinacy** ([AB09, Exercise 4.10]; spec, fill pending —
-phase P4.3): every finite two-person perfect-information game without draws
+/-- G1: the remaining-game value, always from player one's perspective:
+terminal value is `W`, even plies use OR and odd plies use AND. -/
+private def positionValue (W : List Bool → Bool) : ℕ → List Bool → Bool
+  | 0, h => W h
+  | r + 1, h =>
+      if h.length % 2 = 0 then
+        positionValue W r (h ++ [true]) || positionValue W r (h ++ [false])
+      else
+        positionValue W r (h ++ [true]) && positionValue W r (h ++ [false])
+
+/-- G2: append the move prescribed by the current mover's strategy. -/
+private def ply (s₁ s₂ : List Bool → Bool) (h : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  h ++ [if h.length % 2 = 0 then s₁ h else s₂ h]
+
+/-- The recursive play history takes one ply at its successor horizon. -/
+private theorem playOut_succ_ply (s₁ s₂ : List Bool → Bool) (r : ℕ) :
+    playOut s₁ s₂ (r + 1) = ply s₁ s₂ (playOut s₁ s₂ r) := rfl
+
+/-- G2: playing from the empty history is iteration of the one-ply map. -/
+private theorem playOut_eq_iterate (s₁ s₂ : List Bool → Bool) (r : ℕ) :
+    playOut s₁ s₂ r = (ply s₁ s₂)^[r] [] := by
+  induction r with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ r ih => rw [playOut_succ_ply, ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply']
+
+/-- G3: player one takes the true move exactly when that child has true
+value at the remaining horizon. -/
+private def firstGreedy (n : ℕ) (W : List Bool → Bool) (h : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  positionValue W (n - (h.length + 1)) (h ++ [true])
+
+/-- G3: player two takes the true move exactly when that child's value is
+false at the remaining horizon. -/
+private def secondGreedy (n : ℕ) (W : List Bool → Bool) (h : List Bool) : Bool :=
+  !(firstGreedy n W h)
+
+/-- G4: the player selected by the target bit can maintain the current
+value through the remaining play by following its greedy strategy.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the remaining plies. The horizon equation makes
+the greedy look-ahead equal to the child's remaining horizon. At the
+constrained player's turn the greedy move preserves the value. At the
+other player's turn, a false OR or a true AND fixes both child values.
+The induction hypothesis applies to the chosen child. At horizon zero
+position value is the terminal predicate. -/
+private theorem winner_of_value (n : ℕ) (W : List Bool → Bool)
+    (s₁ s₂ : List Bool → Bool) (b : Bool)
+    (hs₁ : b = true → s₁ = firstGreedy n W)
+    (hs₂ : b = false → s₂ = secondGreedy n W)
+    (r : ℕ) (h : List Bool) (hlen : h.length + r = n)
+    (hv : positionValue W r h = b) :
+    W ((ply s₁ s₂)^[r] h) = b := by
+  induction r generalizing h with
+  | zero => exact hv
+  | succ r ih =>
+      have hr : n - (h.length + 1) = r := by omega
+      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
+      refine ih (ply s₁ s₂ h) ?_ ?_
+      · simp only [ply, List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
+        omega
+      · cases b <;> by_cases heven : h.length % 2 = 0 <;>
+          cases htrue : positionValue W r (h ++ [true]) <;>
+          cases hfalse : positionValue W r (h ++ [false]) <;>
+          cases hmove : (if h.length % 2 = 0 then s₁ h else s₂ h) <;>
+          simp_all [positionValue, ply, firstGreedy, secondGreedy]
+
+/-- **Zermelo determinacy** ([AB09, Exercise 4.10]): every finite two-person perfect-information game without draws
 is determined — exactly one quantifier alternation wins, so in particular
 one of the players has a winning strategy.
 
@@ -96,6 +160,16 @@ other — not claimed in this statement, which renders the exercise's "one of
 the two players has a winning strategy" disjunction. -/
 theorem determined (n : ℕ) (W : List Bool → Bool) :
     FirstWins n W ∨ SecondWins n W := by
-  sorry
+  cases hv : positionValue W n [] with
+  | false =>
+      refine Or.inr ⟨secondGreedy n W, fun s₁ => ?_⟩
+      rw [playOut_eq_iterate]
+      exact winner_of_value n W s₁ (secondGreedy n W) false
+        (by simp) (fun _ => rfl) n [] (by simp) hv
+  | true =>
+      refine Or.inl ⟨firstGreedy n W, fun s₂ => ?_⟩
+      rw [playOut_eq_iterate]
+      exact winner_of_value n W (firstGreedy n W) s₂ true
+        (fun _ => rfl) (by simp) n [] (by simp) hv
 
 end Complexity.Game

From 5f492937c7f901b55a4c8888a7985d09415e3641 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/Diagonalization/Relativization.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/Diagonalization/Relativization.lean
index 4634f55b..ea93dbc1 100644
--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/Diagonalization/Relativization.lean
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/Diagonalization/Relativization.lean
@@ -51,7 +51,7 @@ enumeration of deterministic polynomial-time oracle machines so that
 
 * `Complexity.unaryWitnessLang` — the book's `U_B`. [AB09, Theorem 3.7]
 
-## Main results (all sorried; phase-P3.2 statements)
+## Main results (three phase-P3.2 statements remain sorried)
 
 * `Complexity.unaryWitnessLang_mem_NPOracle` — `U_B ∈ NP^B`, for every `B`.
 * `Complexity.exists_finOracleTM_enumeration` — an enumeration of the
@@ -111,6 +111,161 @@ theorem unaryWitnessLang_mem_NPOracle (B : Language Bool) :
     unaryWitnessLang B ∈ NPOracle B := by
   sorry
 
+/-- R1: transport an oracle table along a state equivalence. The ordinary
+transition uses `Action.mapState`; all distinguished states are transported.
+The received relabelling API covers only plain machines, so this oracle
+version is requested for `TuringMachine/Oracle.lean` when a second consumer
+appears. -/
+private def oracleRelabel {k : ℕ} {Symbol S S' : Type*}
+    (tm : OracleTM k Symbol S) (e : S ≃ S') : OracleTM k Symbol S' where
+  q₀ := e tm.q₀
+  qQuery := e tm.qQuery
+  qYes := e tm.qYes
+  qNo := e tm.qNo
+  tr q inp work := (tm.tr (e.symm q) inp work).mapState e
+
+/-- R1: injectivity preserves the three required state inequalities. -/
+private theorem oracleRelabel_wellFormed {k : ℕ} {Symbol S S' : Type*}
+    (tm : OracleTM k Symbol S) (e : S ≃ S') (wf : tm.WellFormed) :
+    (oracleRelabel tm e).WellFormed := by
+  exact ⟨e.injective.ne wf.qQuery_ne_qYes,
+    e.injective.ne wf.qQuery_ne_qNo, e.injective.ne wf.qYes_ne_qNo⟩
+
+/-- R1: one oracle step commutes with state relabelling, including the
+query-answer branch and absorbing halted configurations.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Split the optional state. A halted configuration is fixed.
+At the query state, injectivity identifies the same query branch; the query
+string ignores the state, and mapping the answer commutes with its conditional.
+Elsewhere the inverse equivalence recovers the original table row, and
+`Cfg.mapState_apply` transports its action. This is the single step argument
+used by all later run and behavior transfers. -/
+private theorem oracleRelabel_step {k : ℕ} {Symbol S S' : Type*}
+    {x : List Symbol} (tm : OracleTM k Symbol S) (e : S ≃ S')
+    (O : Language Symbol) (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol S x) :
+    (oracleRelabel tm e).step O (cfg.mapState e) = (tm.step O cfg).mapState e := by
+  classical
+  unfold OracleTM.step
+  cases hs : cfg.state with
+  | none => simp only [Cfg.mapState, hs, Option.map_none]
+  | some q =>
+      simp only [Cfg.mapState, hs, Option.map_some, oracleRelabel, e.injective.eq_iff]
+      by_cases hq : q = tm.qQuery
+      · rw [if_pos hq, if_pos hq]
+        refine Cfg.ext ?_ rfl rfl rfl rfl
+        change some (if OracleTM.queryString cfg ∈ O then e tm.qYes else e tm.qNo) =
+          some (e (if OracleTM.queryString cfg ∈ O then tm.qYes else tm.qNo))
+        rw [apply_ite e]
+      · rw [if_neg hq, if_neg hq]
+        simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using
+          Cfg.mapState_apply e (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols) cfg
+
+/-- R1: arbitrary-start oracle runs commute with state relabelling, by the
+standard iteration theorem applied to the single step commutation. -/
+private theorem oracleRelabel_runFrom {k : ℕ} {Symbol S S' : Type*}
+    {x : List Symbol} (tm : OracleTM k Symbol S) (e : S ≃ S')
+    (O : Language Symbol) (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol S x) (t : ℕ) :
+    (oracleRelabel tm e).runFrom O (cfg.mapState e) t =
+      (tm.runFrom O cfg t).mapState e := by
+  have h : Function.Semiconj (Cfg.mapState (input := x) e)
+      (tm.step O) ((oracleRelabel tm e).step O) :=
+    fun c => (oracleRelabel_step tm e O c).symm
+  exact (h.iterate_right t cfg).symm
+
+/-- R1: relabelling preserves every oracle-relative time-bounded output
+verdict. Initialization transports definitionally; run transport preserves
+output, and `Option.map_eq_none_iff` preserves haltedness. -/
+private theorem oracleRelabel_computesInTime {k : ℕ} {Symbol S S' : Type*}
+    (tm : OracleTM k Symbol S) (e : S ≃ S') (O : Language Symbol)
+    (x out : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
+    (oracleRelabel tm e).ComputesInTime O x out t ↔ tm.ComputesInTime O x out t := by
+  have hinit : (oracleRelabel tm e).initCfg x = (tm.initCfg x).mapState e := rfl
+  simp only [OracleTM.ComputesInTime, hinit, oracleRelabel_runFrom]
+  simp only [Cfg.mapState, Option.map_eq_none_iff]
+
+/-- R2: well-formed binary oracle tables over the canonical state type. -/
+private abbrev CanonTab (k n : ℕ) :=
+  {tm : OracleTM k Bool (Fin n) // tm.WellFormed}
+
+set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1024 in
+/-- R2: one named finiteness structure for canonical tables. All later ranks
+and cardinalities use this structure explicitly to avoid instance diamonds.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Inject the well-formed subtype into the tuple of its four
+state fields and the transition table's four action fields. Each coordinate
+is finite. Tuple injectivity, function extensionality and the two structure
+constructor injectivity lemmas recover the original table. The oracle and
+action layers do not yet supply this finiteness API; its requested shared
+home is `TuringMachine/Oracle.lean` at a second consumer. -/
+private noncomputable def canonTabFintype (k n : ℕ) : Fintype (CanonTab k n) := by
+  let fields : OracleTM k Bool (Fin n) →
+      Fin n × Fin n × Fin n × Fin n ×
+        (Fin n → Option Bool → (Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool) →
+          SignType × (Fin (k + 1) → Option (Option Bool) × SignType) ×
+            Option Bool × Option (Fin n)) :=
+    fun tm => ⟨tm.q₀, tm.qQuery, tm.qYes, tm.qNo, fun q inp work =>
+      ⟨(tm.tr q inp work).inputTape, (tm.tr q inp work).workTapes,
+        (tm.tr q inp work).output, (tm.tr q inp work).state⟩⟩
+  refine Fintype.ofInjective (fun x : CanonTab k n => fields x.val) ?_
+  intro a b hab
+  apply Subtype.ext
+  rcases a with ⟨⟨a₀, aQ, aY, aN, ta⟩, wa⟩
+  rcases b with ⟨⟨b₀, bQ, bY, bN, tb⟩, wb⟩
+  simp only [fields, Prod.mk.injEq] at hab
+  rcases hab with ⟨h₀, hQ, hY, hN, ht⟩
+  simp only [OracleTM.mk.injEq]
+  refine ⟨h₀, hQ, hY, hN, ?_⟩
+  funext q inp work
+  have hrow := congrFun (congrFun (congrFun ht q) inp) work
+  cases ha : ta q inp work
+  cases hb : tb q inp work
+  simpa only [ha, hb, Prod.mk.injEq, Action.mk.injEq] using hrow
+
+/-- R3: the well-formed three-state fallback starts in the yes state and
+halts on its first ordinary transition. No oracle-table default is supplied
+by the construction layer; this explicit table totalizes invalid ranks. -/
+private def oracleDefault : FinOracleTM Bool :=
+  ⟨0, Fin 3, ⟨1, 0, 1, 2, fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩⟩,
+    ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide⟩⟩
+
+/-- R4: select a canonical table at an explicit rank, with the fixed
+fallback for rank overflow. Keeping the three coordinates as arguments lets
+the decoder simplify its pairing before opening the dependent rank branch. -/
+private noncomputable def oracleTableAt (k n r : ℕ) : FinOracleTM Bool :=
+  if h : r < @Fintype.card (CanonTab k n) (canonTabFintype k n) then
+    let table := (@Fintype.equivFin (CanonTab k n) (canonTabFintype k n)).symm ⟨r, h⟩
+    ⟨k, Fin n, table.val, table.property⟩
+  else oracleDefault
+
+/-- R4: decode the tape count, state count and rank using two pairings. -/
+private noncomputable def decodeOracleTable (j : ℕ) : FinOracleTM Bool :=
+  oracleTableAt (Nat.unpair j).1 (Nat.unpair (Nat.unpair j).2).1
+    (Nat.unpair (Nat.unpair j).2).2
+
+/-- R4: the code made from a canonical table's rank decodes to that table.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Unpair the two coordinates. The rank's `Fin.isLt` proof
+selects the valid branch without computing the cardinality. The inverse
+law of the same explicitly instantiated equivalence recovers the table. -/
+private theorem decodeOracleTable_rank (k n : ℕ) (table : CanonTab k n) :
+    decodeOracleTable (Nat.pair k (Nat.pair n
+      ((@Fintype.equivFin (CanonTab k n) (canonTabFintype k n)) table).val)) =
+      (⟨k, Fin n, table.val, table.property⟩ : FinOracleTM Bool) := by
+  simp only [decodeOracleTable, Nat.unpair_pair]
+  rw [oracleTableAt, dif_pos ((@Fintype.equivFin (CanonTab k n) (canonTabFintype k n)) table).isLt]
+  exact congrArg
+    (fun a : CanonTab k n => (⟨k, Fin n, a.val, a.property⟩ : FinOracleTM Bool))
+    ((@Fintype.equivFin (CanonTab k n) (canonTabFintype k n)).symm_apply_apply table)
+
+/-- R5: forget the second coordinate, so every decoded table is repeated. -/
+private noncomputable def oracleEnumeration (i : ℕ) : FinOracleTM Bool :=
+  decodeOracleTable (Nat.unpair i).1
+
+/-- R5: every repetition coordinate yields the same decoded table. -/
+private theorem oracleEnumeration_pair (j r : ℕ) :
+    oracleEnumeration (Nat.pair j r) = decodeOracleTable j := by
+  simp only [oracleEnumeration, Nat.unpair_pair]
+
 /-- **Enumeration of the deterministic finite oracle machines with infinite
 recurrence** [BGS75, p. 432]: there is a family `N : ℕ → Turing.FinOracleTM
 Bool` such that every finite oracle machine `M` recurs at arbitrarily late
@@ -149,14 +304,39 @@ state. Fill obligations, named for the brief: the `OracleTM` relabelling lemma

 across the configuration bijection (`Turing.Cfg.mapState` preserves
 haltedness and output, as in `Turing.exists_codeTM`); the arithmetic of the
-four-coordinate pairing (round-2 finding 2). -/
+four-coordinate pairing (round-2 finding 2).
+

+count `n`, including the empty table types at small counts; invalid ranks

+  intro O x output t

+  rw [oracleEnumeration_pair, htable]

@@ -64,6 +64,8 @@ up, in `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NTIME`, because they fix the binary alphabet.
   under a choice word. [AB09, §2.1.2]
 * `Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin` — every choice word of length `t` halts the machine on the
   given input; the totality condition of [AB09]'s "runs in `T(n)` time".
+* `Turing.NDTM.fixChoice` — the deterministic slice at a fixed choice bit, with
+  `Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step` (added 2026-10-10).
 * `Turing.FinNDTM` — the bundled finite layer, mirroring `Turing.FinTM`.
 * `Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM`, `Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM` — a deterministic machine as an
   NDTM whose two transition functions coincide.
@@ -147,6 +149,21 @@ lemma runWith_append (w w' : List Bool) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
   | nil => rfl
   | cons b w ih => rw [List.cons_append, runWith_cons, runWith_cons, ih]
 
+/-- The deterministic slice of a nondeterministic machine at a fixed choice bit: the
+multi-tape machine that always uses the transition function `tm.tr b`. [AB09, §2.1.2: an
+NDTM has two transition functions, and a choice bit selects one] (Shared by the
+configuration-graph layer; added 2026-10-10.) -/
+def fixChoice (tm : NDTM k Symbol State) (b : Bool) : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State :=
+  ⟨tm.q₀, tm.tr b⟩
+
+/-- One nondeterministic step under the choice bit `b` is one step of the slice at `b`.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Both steps fix a halted configuration, and otherwise apply the action
+that `tm.tr b` reads from the same configuration (`cases` on the state). -/
+theorem stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step (tm : NDTM k Symbol State) (b : Bool)
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : tm.stepWith b cfg = (tm.fixChoice b).step cfg := by
+  cases h : cfg.state <;> simp only [NDTM.stepWith, MultiTapeTM.step, fixChoice, h]
+
 /-- Stepping a halted configuration is the identity, under either choice. -/
 @[simp]
 lemma stepWith_of_halt {b : Bool} {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.state = none) :

--- /dev/null
+++ b/audits/evidence/ch34-s1/S1aPreShip.lean.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+open Turing
+
+/-! S1a pre-ship probe (maintainer, before issue; base `29aa75be`).
+
+Part P declares the four pre-issue promotion candidates with their proofs, at
+the names and homes the brief cites:
+* `Turing.NDTM.fixChoice`, `Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step`
+  → `TuringMachine/Nondeterministic.lean`;
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps`,
+  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none`
+  → `SpaceComplexity/ConfigCount.lean`, beside `exists_eq_of_between`.
+
+Part P also shows that the two deterministic lemmas re-derive verbatim as
+instances. Their bodies become one-line citations, so no text is duplicated.
+Once Part P has landed, delete it: Part S must still elaborate unchanged
+against the promoted names.
+
+Part S holds the call shapes of the four S1a routes. Its helpers are shapes,
+not the fill: the batch writes its own `private` versions in `ConfigGraph.lean`. -/
+
+/-! ## Part P (landed): the four promoted declarations, and the two re-derived originals -/
+
+#print axioms Turing.NDTM.fixChoice
+#print axioms Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step
+#print axioms Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps
+#print axioms Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none
+#print axioms Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited
+#print axioms Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none
+
+/-! ## Part S — the S1a call shapes -/
+
+namespace Turing.NDTM
+variable {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
+
+-- Shared prefix-step shape (routes 1 and 3): a prefix grows by `w[j]?`.
+theorem probe_runWith_take_succ (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool S x)
+    (j : ℕ) : tm.runWith (w.take (j + 1)) c = tm.runWith (w[j]?).toList (tm.runWith (w.take j) c) := by
+  rw [List.take_succ, NDTM.runWith_append]
+
+theorem probe_take_succ_step (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (j : ℕ) :
+    tm.runWith (w.take (j + 1)) c = tm.runWith (w.take j) c ∨
+      ∃ a : Action k Bool S, tm.runWith (w.take (j + 1)) c = a.apply (tm.runWith (w.take j) c) := by
+  rw [probe_runWith_take_succ]
+  cases w[j]? with
+  | none => exact Or.inl rfl
+  | some b =>
+    simp only [Option.toList_some, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.runWith_nil, NDTM.stepWith]
+    cases (tm.runWith (w.take j) c).state with
+    | none => exact Or.inl rfl
+    | some q => exact Or.inr ⟨_, rfl⟩
+
+-- Route 3, window: both ND facts are instances of the promoted generic lemmas.
+theorem probe_abs_lt_card_visitedWith (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (i : Fin k)
+    {z : ℤ} (hz : z ∈ tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i) :
+    |z| < (tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i).card :=
+  MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps
+    (fun j => (tm.runWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x)).workTapePos i) (by simp)
+    (fun j => by
+      rcases probe_take_succ_step tm w (tm.initCfg x) j with h | ⟨a, h⟩
+      · simp only [h, sub_self, abs_zero, zero_le_one]
+      · simp only [h]; exact workTapePos_apply_le a _ i) w.length hz
+
+theorem probe_mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (i : Fin k)
+    (z : ℤ) (hz : (tm.runWith w (tm.initCfg x)).workTapes i z ≠ none) :
+    z ∈ tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i :=
+  MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none
+    (fun j => tm.runWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x)) (by simp)
+    (fun j => probe_take_succ_step tm w (tm.initCfg x) j) w.length i z
+    (by simpa only [List.take_length] using hz)
+
+-- Route 3: a single prefix's space is within the whole word's (the window's source).
+example (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (i : Fin k) :
+    (tm.visitedWith w c i).card ≤ tm.spaceUsedWith w c :=
+  Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun i => (tm.visitedWith w c i).card)
+    (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i)
+
+-- Route 2: the core half cites `core_step` through the slice.
+theorem probe_outputSymbol_congr (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
+    (h : MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core c = MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core d) :
+    M.outputSymbol c = M.outputSymbol d := by
+  simp only [MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
+  obtain ⟨hs, hi, hw, hp⟩ := h
+  have hsym : c.inputSymbol = d.inputSymbol := by unfold Cfg.inputSymbol; simp only [hi]
+  have hws : c.workTapeSymbols = d.workTapeSymbols := by
+    funext i; simp only [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, hw, hp]
+  unfold MultiTapeTM.outputSymbol
+  rw [hs, hsym, hws]
+
+example (c : Cfg k Bool S x) :
+    coreSum c = (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core c, outSummary c.output) := rfl
+
+end Turing.NDTM
+
+namespace Turing
+
+-- Route 2 / audit Q1: the summary is an append congruence (audit §7 sanity items).
+theorem probe_outSummary_eq_accept_iff (u : List Bool) : outSummary u = .accept ↔ u = [true] := by
+  match u with
+  | [] => simp [outSummary]
+  | [true] => simp [outSummary]
+  | [false] => simp [outSummary]
+  | _ :: _ :: _ => simp [outSummary]
+
+theorem probe_outSummary_append_congr {u v : List Bool} (h : outSummary u = outSummary v)
+    (e : List Bool) : outSummary (u ++ e) = outSummary (v ++ e) := by
+  have key : ∀ u : List Bool, (outSummary u = .empty ↔ u = []) ∧
+      (outSummary u = .accept ↔ u = [true]) := by
+    intro u
+    match u with
+    | [] => simp [outSummary]
+    | [true] => simp [outSummary]
+    | [false] => simp [outSummary]
+    | _ :: _ :: _ => simp [outSummary]
+  have dead : ∀ u e : List Bool, outSummary u = .dead → outSummary (u ++ e) = .dead := by
+    intro u e hu
+    cases hs : outSummary (u ++ e) with
+    | dead => rfl
+    | empty =>
+      have := ((key _).1.mp hs); simp only [List.append_eq_nil_iff] at this
+      rw [this.1] at hu; simp [outSummary] at hu
+    | accept =>
+      have h1 := (key _).2.mp hs
+      rcases u with _ | ⟨a, u⟩
+      · simp [outSummary] at hu
+      · rcases u with _ | ⟨b, u⟩
+        · simp only [List.cons_append, List.nil_append, List.cons.injEq] at h1
+          rw [h1.1] at hu; simp [outSummary] at hu
+        · simp at h1
+  cases hu : outSummary u with
+  | empty =>
+    rw [hu] at h; rw [(key _).1.mp hu, (key _).1.mp h.symm]
+  | accept =>
+    rw [hu] at h; rw [(key _).2.mp hu, (key _).2.mp h.symm]
+  | dead =>
+    rw [hu] at h; rw [dead u e hu, dead v e h.symm]
+
+-- Route 2 composes: slice + `core_step` + `step_output` + the congruence.
+example {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (b : Bool)
+    {c d : Cfg k Bool S x} (h : NDTM.coreSum c = NDTM.coreSum d) :
+    NDTM.coreSum (tm.stepWith b c) = NDTM.coreSum (tm.stepWith b d) := by
+  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, Prod.mk.injEq] at h ⊢
+  obtain ⟨hc, hs⟩ := h
+  rw [NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step]
+  refine ⟨MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step _ hc, ?_⟩
+  rw [MultiTapeTM.step_output, MultiTapeTM.step_output, NDTM.probe_outputSymbol_congr _ hc]
+  exact probe_outSummary_append_congr hs _
+
+end Turing
+
+-- Route 3: `coreCode_inj` under the window hypotheses.
+example {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (B : ℕ) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
+    (hc : ∀ i, |c.workTapePos i| ≤ B ∧ ∀ z, c.workTapes i z ≠ none → |z| ≤ B)
+    (hd : ∀ i, |d.workTapePos i| ≤ B ∧ ∀ z, d.workTapes i z ≠ none → |z| ≤ B)
+    (h : MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode B c = MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode B d) :
+    MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core c = MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core d :=
+  MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj B hc hd h
+
+-- Route 3: the code universe, with the summary coded in `Fin 3`, has exactly `configBound`
+-- elements (`OutSummary` has no `Fintype` instance).
+example (N : FinNDTM Bool) (n s : ℕ) :
+    Fintype.card ((Option N.State × Fin (n + 2) × (Fin N.k → Fin (2 * s + 1) → Option Bool) ×
+      (Fin N.k → Fin (2 * s + 1))) × Fin 3) = N.configBound n s := by
+  simp only [Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_option, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_pi,
+    Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_bool, FinNDTM.configBound]
+  rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm (2 * s + 1) N.k]
+  ring
+
+-- Route 3: the injection-to-count shape (as in `of_spaceUsed_le`).
+example {α : Type} [Fintype α] (f : ℕ → α) (T : ℕ)
+    (hinj : Set.InjOn f (Finset.range T : Set ℕ)) : T ≤ Fintype.card α := by
+  have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn f (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ (f a)) hinj
+  simpa using this
+
+-- Routes 3 and 4: padding.
+example (N : FinNDTM Bool) {x : List Bool} {t t' : ℕ} (h : N.AcceptsWithin x t)
+    (hle : t ≤ t') : N.AcceptsWithin x t' := h.mono hle
+
+-- Route 4: truncation to the deciding budget.
+example {k : ℕ} {S : Type} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (x w : List Bool) (T : ℕ)
+    (hH : tm.HaltsWithin x T) (hT : T ≤ w.length) :
+    tm.runWith w (tm.initCfg x) = tm.runWith (w.take T) (tm.initCfg x) := by
+  have hp := hH (w.take T) (List.length_take_of_le hT)
+  conv_lhs => rw [← List.take_append_drop T w]
+  rw [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_of_halt _ hp]
+
+-- Route 4: `DecidesInSpace` unpacks to the three conjuncts.
+example (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) (h : N.DecidesInSpace L s)
+    (x : List Bool) : ∃ T, N.tm.HaltsWithin x T ∧
+      (∀ w : List Bool, w.length = T → N.tm.spaceUsedWith w (N.tm.initCfg x) ≤ s x.length) ∧
+      (x ∈ L ↔ N.AcceptsWithin x T) := h x
+
+-- Route 1: the two directions' step shapes.
+example {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) (b : Bool)
+    (c : Cfg k Bool S x) : tm.runWith (w ++ [b]) c = tm.stepWith b (tm.runWith w c) := by
+  rw [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.runWith_nil]
+example {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (b : Bool)
+    {c c' : Cfg k Bool S x} (h : Relation.ReflTransGen tm.CfgStep (tm.stepWith b c) c') :
+    Relation.ReflTransGen tm.CfgStep c c' := Relation.ReflTransGen.head ⟨b, rfl⟩ h
+
+-- Optional exports E1–E4 (audit §7): the exact statements the brief sanctions.
+namespace Turing
+theorem probe_E3_coreSum_runWith {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S)
+    (w : List Bool) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x} (h : NDTM.coreSum c = NDTM.coreSum d) :
+    NDTM.coreSum (tm.runWith w c) = NDTM.coreSum (tm.runWith w d) := by
+  induction w generalizing c d with
+  | nil => exact h
+  | cons b w ih => exact ih (NDTM.coreSum_stepWith tm b h)
+
+theorem probe_E4_not_acceptsWithin_zero (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) :
+    ¬ N.AcceptsWithin x 0 := by
+  rintro ⟨w, hw, hs, -⟩
+  rw [List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp hw] at hs
+  simp at hs
+end Turing
+
+-- The four frozen S1a targets, and the three summit statements, elaborate (sorried at issue).
+#check @NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff
+#check @NDTM.coreSum_stepWith
+#check @FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le
+#check @FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound
+#check @Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime
+#check @Complexity.NL_subset_P
+#check @Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL
+
+-- Cited infrastructure and the promotion candidates: within the standard triple.
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.exists_eq_of_between
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.step_output
+#print axioms Turing.workTapePos_apply_le
+#print axioms FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono
+#print axioms NDTM.runWith_append
+#print axioms NDTM.runWith_of_halt
+#print axioms NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps
+#print axioms MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none

+'Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+@NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff : ∀ {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (c c' : Cfg k Bool S x),
+  Relation.ReflTransGen tm.CfgStep c c' ↔ ∃ w, NDTM.runWith w c = c'
+@NDTM.coreSum_stepWith : ∀ {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (b : Bool) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x},
+  NDTM.coreSum c = NDTM.coreSum d → NDTM.coreSum (NDTM.stepWith b c) = NDTM.coreSum (NDTM.stepWith b d)
+FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le : ∀ (N : FinNDTM Bool) {x : List Bool} {T s : ℕ},
+  N.AcceptsWithin x T →
+    (∀ (w : List Bool), w.length = T → N.tm.spaceUsedWith w (NDTM.initCfg x) ≤ s) →
+      N.AcceptsWithin x (N.configBound x.length s)
+@FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound : ∀ {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {s : ℕ → ℕ},
+  N.DecidesInSpace L s → ∀ (x : List Bool), x ∈ L ↔ N.AcceptsWithin x (N.configBound x.length (s x.length))
+Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime : ∀ (S : ℕ → ℕ),
+  Complexity.SpaceConstructible S → Complexity.NSPACE S ⊆ ⋃ c, Complexity.DTIME fun n => 2 ^ (c * (S n + 1))
+Complexity.NL_subset_P : Complexity.NL ⊆ Complexity.P
+Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL : ∀ (L : Language Bool),
+  (∃ y, y ∈ L) → (∃ z, z ∉ L) → ∀ {L' : Language Bool}, L' ∈ Complexity.NL → Complexity.PolyTimeReducible L' L
+'Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]

+'Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.exists_eq_of_between' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+'Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_output' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]
+'Turing.workTapePos_apply_le' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+'Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]
+'Turing.NDTM.runWith_append' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]

diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/NTIME.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/NTIME.lean
index 4a7c6d8c..bf0108d2 100644
--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/NTIME.lean
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/NTIME.lean
@@ -71,6 +71,9 @@ deterministic embedding `DTIME ⊆ NTIME`.
 * `Complexity.NTIME.mono` — `NTIME` is monotone in the time bound.
 * `Complexity.DTIME_subset_NTIME` — deterministic time is nondeterministic time.
   [AB09, §2.1.2]
+* `Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM_haltsWithin_and_accepts_iff` — its per-input content, a
+  deterministic decider run nondeterministically (shared with `SPACE ⊆ NSPACE`;
+  added 2026-10-10).
 * `Complexity.NTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero` — a vanishing time bound gives the empty
   class, as for `DTIME`.
 
@@ -119,6 +122,47 @@ def DecidesInTime (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Pro
 
 end Turing.FinNDTM
 
+namespace Turing.FinTM
+
+/-- **A deterministic decider, run nondeterministically.** If `M` halts on `x` within `t`
+steps with output `[x ∈ L]`, then every branch of `M.toFinNDTM` of length `t` halts, and
+`M.toFinNDTM` accepts `x` within `t` exactly when `x ∈ L`. This is the per-input content
+of `Complexity.DTIME_subset_NTIME`, shared with the space inclusion
+`Complexity.SPACE_subset_NSPACE`. [AB09, §2.1.2: a TM is an NDTM that ignores its
+choices]
+
+**Proof sketch.** By `Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith`, the run under **any** choice
+word of length `t` is `M`'s deterministic run to time `t` (`Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff`
+unfolds the hypothesis). So every branch of length `t` is halted. A member is accepted by
+`List.replicate t false`, whose run ends with output `[true]`. For a non-member every
+branch ends with output `[false] ≠ [true]` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator`), so no branch
+accepts. -/
+theorem toFinNDTM_haltsWithin_and_accepts_iff (M : FinTM Bool) {L : Language Bool}
+    {x : List Bool} {t : ℕ}
+    (h : M.ComputesInTime x [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x] t) :
+    M.toFinNDTM.tm.HaltsWithin x t ∧ (x ∈ L ↔ M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t) := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨hhalt, hout⟩ := (M.computesInTime_iff _ _ _).mp h
+  have hrun (w : List Bool) :
+      M.toFinNDTM.tm.runWith w (M.toFinNDTM.tm.initCfg x) =
+        M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) w.length :=
+    M.tm.toNDTM_runWith w (M.tm.initCfg x)
+  refine ⟨fun w hw => ?_, fun hx => ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [hrun, hw]
+    exact hhalt
+  · refine ⟨List.replicate t false, List.length_replicate .., ?_, ?_⟩
+    · rw [hrun, List.length_replicate]
+      exact hhalt
+    · rw [hrun, List.length_replicate, hout]
+      simp only [MultiTapeTM.indicator, if_pos hx]
+  · rintro ⟨w, hw, _, hwout⟩
+    rw [hrun, hw, hout] at hwout
+    by_contra hx
+    simp only [MultiTapeTM.indicator, if_neg hx] at hwout
+    cases hwout
+
+end Turing.FinTM
+
 namespace Complexity
 
 open Turing
@@ -166,40 +210,12 @@ theorem NTIME.mono {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, T₁ n ≤ T₂ n) : NT
 that ignores its choices, so `DTIME T ⊆ NTIME T`.

-`Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM M`. By `Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith`, the run under
-**any** choice word of length `t` is `M`'s deterministic run to time `t`, so: every
-branch of length `c · T n` is halted because `M`'s computation has halted by then
-(`Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime` unfolded through `Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff`),
-giving `HaltsWithin`; and some branch of that length is halted with output `[true]` iff
-`M`'s output at that time is `[true]`, which by the indicator contract
-(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator`) holds iff `x ∈ L` — for `x ∉ L` the output is
-`[false] ≠ [true]` on every branch, so no branch accepts. -/
+`Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM M`. On each input, `M`'s computation of the indicator by time
+`c · T n` gives both clauses of `Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime` at once, by

-  classical

-      refine ⟨List.replicate (c * T x.length) false, List.length_replicate .., ?_, ?_⟩

+/-- A machine with no work tapes computes in zero space whatever it computes at all: the
+space measure counts only work-tape cells. (Shared by the zero-space layer; added
+2026-10-10.)
+
+**Proof sketch.** With `M.k = 0` the space measure is an empty sum
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero`), at every halting time. -/
+theorem computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero {M : FinTM Bool} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hk : M.k = 0) (h : ∀ x, ∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x (f x) t) :
+    M.ComputesInSpace f fun _ => 0 := by
+  intro x
+  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h x
+  exact ⟨t, ht, (MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero (tm := M.tm) _ t hk).le⟩
+
 end Turing.FinTM
 
 namespace Complexity

   rintro L ⟨c, M, hM⟩
   exact ⟨c, M, hM.mono fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)⟩
 
+/-- `SPACE` absorbs constant factors: if `s₁ ≤ a · s₂` pointwise, then
+`SPACE s₁ ⊆ SPACE s₂`. [AB09, Def 4.1: the constant `c` absorbs `a`] (Shared by the
+zero-space layer and the hierarchy arguments; added 2026-10-10.)
+
+**Proof sketch.** A witness at constant `c` for `s₁` is a witness at constant `c · a`
+for `s₂`, since `c · s₁ n ≤ c · (a · s₂ n) = (c · a) · s₂ n`
+(`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono`). -/
+theorem SPACE.mono_const {s₁ s₂ : ℕ → ℕ} {a : ℕ} (h : ∀ n, s₁ n ≤ a * s₂ n) :
+    SPACE s₁ ⊆ SPACE s₂ := by
+  rintro L ⟨c, M, hM⟩
+  refine ⟨c * a, M, hM.mono fun n => ?_⟩
+  calc c * s₁ n ≤ c * (a * s₂ n) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)
+    _ = c * a * s₂ n := (Nat.mul_assoc c a (s₂ n)).symm
+
 /-- The logarithmic space bound `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`: `Θ(log n)`, and at least `1`, following the
 convention `s(n) ≥ log n` of [AB09, p. 79]. -/
 def logSpace (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log 2 n + 1
diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/NSPACE.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/NSPACE.lean
index c37291d7..ca41531c 100644
--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/NSPACE.lean
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/NSPACE.lean
@@ -38,6 +38,12 @@ branch-space measure (`Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith`).
   every branch's space, so longer words add nothing.
 * Constants are absorbed as `c · s n`, and there is **no** `s(n) ≥ log n` side
   condition, as for `Complexity.SPACE`.
+* **Zero bounds collapse the class, as for `Complexity.SPACE`** (P4.1 statement
+  gate, note 6): every branch visits each work tape's initial head cell, so a zero
+  of the bound at any input length forces the witness to have no work tapes at all.
+  The normalized classes (`n ^ c + 1`, `Complexity.logSpace`) are positive
+  everywhere and are unaffected. The `NSPACE` sanity twins (tape-count bound,
+  collapse, normalization) are a recorded future additive layer.

 ## References
 
@@ -69,7 +71,7 @@ sites.
 namespace Turing
 
 /-!
-### Raw-layer output lemmas
+### Raw-layer output and space lemmas
 
 Additions on top of the vendored files (kept here so the vendored `Deterministic.lean`
 stays byte-comparable with upstream).
@@ -115,6 +117,23 @@ theorem output_prefix (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol Stat
     rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.step_output]
     exact ih.trans (List.prefix_append _ _)
 
+/-- A run of `t` steps visits at most `t + 1` cells on each work tape, hence at most
+`k · (t + 1)` cells in all. [AB09, proof of Theorem 4.2: a machine running in time `T`
+visits at most `T` cells per tape, up to the starting cell]
+
+**Proof sketch.** Each tape's visited set is the image of `Finset.range (t + 1)`
+(`Finset.card_image_le`, `Finset.card_range`); sum over the `k` tapes
+(`Finset.sum_le_sum`, `Finset.sum_const_nat`). -/
+theorem spaceUsed_le_mul_succ (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
+    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
+    tm.spaceUsed cfg t ≤ k * (t + 1) := by
+  calc tm.spaceUsed cfg t = ∑ i, tm.spaceUsedByTape cfg t i := rfl
+    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin k, (t + 1) := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => by
+      unfold MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead
+      exact (Finset.card_image_le).trans (Finset.card_range (t + 1)).le
+    _ = k * (t + 1) := by
+      rw [Finset.sum_const_nat fun _ _ => rfl, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
+
 end MultiTapeTM
 
 /-- A multi-tape Turing machine over the alphabet `Option Symbol` bundled with a finite

## ===== audits/evidence/ch34-c1/patches/s1a-0001-Prove-the-S1a-configuration-graph-lemmas.patch =====

From 99be7d9a6c7c6ea80cdd2eb2b2a3c93e6ecca134 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Codex <codex@openai.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 02:37:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] Prove the S1a configuration graph lemmas

---
 .../SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph.lean          | 332 +++++++++++++++++-
 1 file changed, 319 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-)

diff --git a/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph.lean b/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph.lean
index cc753f05..837eb231 100644
--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph.lean
+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph.lean
@@ -26,8 +26,8 @@ polynomial-time reductions below `P` ([AB09, Exercise 4.3]). This is phase P4.2
 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`; Savitch's theorem, the other consumer of
 this layer, is `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Savitch`.
 
-**Status: statement skeleton (phase P4.2).** Definitions are real; every
-contract is sorried with a sketch naming its fill obligations.
+**Status: graph lemmas proved (phase P4.2, batch S1a).** The four graph
+contracts are proved; the three class results remain sorried for S1b.
 
 ## Design
 
@@ -62,7 +62,7 @@ contract is sorried with a sketch naming its fill obligations.
 * `Turing.FinNDTM.configBound` — the vertex count at window radius `s`:
   three times the deterministic `configBound` formula. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]
 
-## Main results (all sorried; phase-P4.2 statements)
+## Main results (graph lemmas proved; three class results sorried)
 
 * `Turing.NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff` — reachability is the choice-word run.
